(6) Data och kod anger commit för kontrollen i 4.5 och byggskriptet för version 3 (6eae0af). (7) Ändringar som version 3 gjorde men inte skrev in i loggen: svagheten om vägens ålder säger inte längre att en sentida väg bara kan försvaga sambandet, eftersom en väg som dragits förbi stenarna eller en sten som ställts upp mot en nyare väg också kan stärka det; 5.2 anger Rayleighs test i var halva; steget med den rättade regeln för flyttade stenar säger att huvudanalysen redan bygger på den regeln, och 4.4 och 5.3 anger regeln med datumet för rättelsen; meningen under Data och kod om en kommande release med DOI är struken.
posts.title_en: The runestones turned their text towards the road – half of the inscriptions within 45 degrees of the road, against a quarter expected
posts.summary_en: Pre-registered study. Of the runestones that still stand in place and where we know where the road ran, half turn the inscription towards the road, against a quarter if the direction were random. The finding holds in both halves of the material and in every sensitivity analysis, also when two coding errors are corrected. The text was turned towards those passing by; we found no consistent sign that it was turned towards a particular point of the compass or towards the farm.
posts.body_en:
*Viktor Kvant, independent researcher. Fully tested finding. Report version 4, 2026-11-05 (first published 2026-10-31). Timeline: the analysis plan was locked 2026-10-29; the analysis was run 2026-10-29; the addendum plan for the sensitivity analyses was locked and run 2026-10-31; a review before archiving found two coding errors 2026-11-05; the check with corrected directions was run 2026-11-05. The analysis was made in Vitki 3.0.0. Licence CC BY 4.0. This English version is the canonical one for citation: Kvant, V. (2026). The runestones turned their text towards the road – half of the inscriptions within 45 degrees of the road, against a quarter expected. Research report, report version 4; analysis in Vitki 3.0.0. https://vitkirunor.se/en/forskningsrapporter/ristningen-vand-mot-vagen. Keywords: runestones, Viking Age, roads, placement, orientation of the inscription, circular statistics, Swedish register of ancient monuments, pre-registration. Competing interests: none. Funding: none.*

## Abstract

**Background and aim.** Where the runestones were raised has long been discussed, and the roads are one of the answers: stones by roads were seen. Single stones have been described as turned towards the road, but nobody has measured across the whole material which way the inscription was turned. The question here is whether the text was turned towards the road, towards the farm or towards a particular point of the compass.
**Material.** 219 records in the Swedish register of ancient monuments on 214 Swedish Viking-Age runestones that still stand in place and for which the register gives the direction the inscription faces. For 123 of the records there is a road to measure against, for 94 a farm site.
**Method.** A pre-registered study with four tests and Holm correction. The measure is the cosine of the angle between the inscription's direction and the direction to the road, compared with 9,999 shuffles of the directions within the province. Internal replication in two halves and ten sensitivity analyses under a locked addendum plan.
**Results.** Half of the stones, 50 percent, turn the inscription within 45 degrees of the road, against a quarter if the direction were random. Mean cos 0.37 against 0.01 expected, p = 0.0001, Holm-corrected p = 0.0004. It holds in both halves and in every sensitivity analysis, also without Uppland, parish by parish, with one stone per carver and without re-erected stones. Two coding errors found after publication do not change this; corrected, the association is slightly stronger (mean cos 0.39, 52 percent within 45 degrees; section 4.5). The directions do not differ detectably from an even spread, and we found no sign that the inscription was turned towards the farm (farm sites are known only from 17th–18th-century maps).
**Conclusion.** The text was turned towards those passing by on the road. The main weakness is that the road in the register is often today's road; with only registered older routes and road markers the association is weak (28 percent within 45 degrees against 25 expected) but goes the same way.

## 1. Introduction

Gunnar Ekholm (1950) asked where the runestones were raised and answered that the stones of Uppland largely stand by the roads and waterways of the past, and that the stones at grave fields, too, are often explained by the road that passed the grave field. He noted that single stones are turned towards the road, at Bollsta in Vaksala (p. 138) and on Särsta land in Knivsta (p. 139), and that a re-erection can turn a stone: a stone on Ängby land near Knivsta has faced the railway since it was raised again in the 1860s (p. 140). Torun Zachrisson (1998) has related the stones to farm, boundary and grave field, and Lydia Klos (2009) has argued that most were raised at grave fields. Mats G. Larsson (2010, p. 252) has objected that the grave fields are thereby strongly overstated at the expense of other locations; he also notes that Klos used considerably more restrictive criteria than his own earlier survey for what counts as an ancient road (p. 250; see also McLeod 2014). Johan Bollaert (2016) compared stones along three Viking-Age roads with other stones in the same districts and found that the stones by the roads more often have striking ornament and more often belong to monuments of several stones, which supports that they were raised to be seen.

What is missing is a measure across the whole material of how the inscription itself was turned. Ekholm's observations concern single stones, and a stone may stand by a road but turn its text another way. The aim here is to test whether the inscription was turned towards the road, towards the farm or towards a particular point of the compass, with the information on the inscription's direction that the register gives for some stones.

## 2. Pre-registration: hypothesis and plan

The hypotheses, measures and rules of interpretation were written down in an analysis plan on 29 October 2026, before any direction had been computed. The plan has the SHA-256 checksum `cd73b962457fde0e…` (see Data and code). Before locking only the number of records was known: 456 records in the register give a direction, 369 concern a single stone with one direction, 219 of these stand in place, and 88 of the 369 mention a road with a compass point.

The plan tests four hypotheses with Holm correction: H1 that the directions are not evenly spread over the compass, H2 that the inscription is turned towards the road, H3 that it is turned towards the farm and H4 that bridge and road stones are turned towards the road more than others. A hypothesis *holds* when Holm p is below 0.05 and the direction is the same with p below 0.05 in both halves.

The plan did not contain the project's fixed sensitivity analyses, which are built for associations between two traits and not for directions. The corresponding steps for directions were therefore fixed in an addendum plan on 31 October 2026 (SHA-256 `4da9710de49fa2b6…`), before they were computed. Two of the steps, the halves and the source of the road, were already in the main plan. A check of re-erected stones was made after the main run on 29 October with a different word list; in the addendum plan the word list was locked before the step was computed.

## 3. Material

- **The stones.** Swedish Viking-Age runestones in the Scandinavian Runic-text Database (Rundata) that still stand in place and have a known location, and whose record in the Swedish National Heritage Board's register of ancient monuments concerns just that stone and gives one direction with the words "faces" and one of sixteen compass points: 219 records, which concern 214 stones (five stones have two records each and were counted twice in the locked analysis; see 4.5). Runestones only.
- **The road.** First the register's own statement of the stone's position relative to a road ("5 m E of road"; the road then lies in the opposite direction): 69 stones. Otherwise the nearest registered route or road marker within 500 metres. 123 stones with a road in all. The roads come from the National Heritage Board's register only.
- **The farm.** The nearest registered village or farm site within one kilometre: 94 stones.
- **The directions** are computed as bearings from the stone, with north as 0 degrees and the compass points in steps of 22.5 degrees.
- **The halves** are the project's fixed division parish by parish.

## 4. Method

**4.1 The measure.** For each stone the cosine of the angle between the inscription's direction and the direction to the road is computed: 1 when the inscription faces the road straight on, 0 when it faces sideways and −1 when it faces away. The mean over the stones is compared with 9,999 shuffles in which the inscriptions' directions are redistributed among the stones within the same province, so that each province's general pattern of directions is kept. The test is one-sided. The share of stones within 45 degrees of the road is also reported; if the direction were random it would be a quarter.

**4.2 The other hypotheses.** H1 is tested with Rayleigh's test of uniformity (Mardia & Jupp 2000). H3 is tested like H2 against the direction to the farm. H4 compares the mean cos towards the road between bridge and road stones and the others, with the label shuffled within the province, two-sided.

**4.3 Correction and replication.** Holm correction (Holm 1979) over the four tests. Each hypothesis is also tested in each half on its own.

**4.4 The sensitivity analyses** under the addendum plan: the halves; without one province at a time (provinces with at least ten stones with a road; significance required only where at least two thirds of the stones remain); the parish as the unit, with one value per parish; one stone per secure carver; without re-erected stones; without stones the National Heritage Board's register Runor (2020) gives as moved; with the rule for moved stones after the correction of 27 October 2026 (see Data and code); only roads from the register text; and only registered routes and road markers. A step holds when the mean cos lies above the expected value and p is below 0.05.

**4.5 Deviations from the plan.** The analysis followed the plan, but a review before archiving (5 November 2026) found two coding errors in how the register text was read. The numbers in the results section are those of the locked analysis and have not been changed; the errors and a check made afterwards are reported here.

- **Gon qualifiers.** Nine road bearings and six inscription bearings with a gon qualifier ("V 40cg S", that is 40 gon or 36 degrees from west towards south; a gon is one four-hundredth of a full turn) were read as a single compass point. This concerns 9 of the 69 roads from the register text, with errors of 50–86 degrees, and 6 of the 219 inscription directions, with errors of 9–40 degrees. Corrected, the association is slightly stronger: mean cos 0.39 instead of 0.37 and 52 percent within 45 degrees instead of 50; with only roads from the register text 0.53 instead of 0.49.
- **Double records.** Five stones have two records each in the register and were counted twice; the 219 records concern 214 stones, and the 123 with a road concern 120. Counting each stone once, with corrected directions, gives mean cos 0.37 and 51 percent within 45 degrees.
- **The check.** With the corrected directions the main test and every sensitivity analysis were rerun with the same code and the same shuffles as under the plans; with the old directions the code reproduces the published numbers exactly. Every step holds, both with the 219 records and with each stone counted once. The main test gives p = 0.0001, half B p = 0.003 and 0.008 respectively, and the weakest step, only registered routes and road markers, p = 0.024 and 0.047. H1 and H3 do not change in substance (Rayleigh's test p = 0.46; towards the farm p = 0.29).

## 5. Results

**5.1 Towards the road (H2).** Of the 123 records with a road (120 stones; see 4.5), 50 percent turn the inscription within 45 degrees of the road. The mean cos is 0.37 against 0.01 expected, p = 0.0001, the lowest value 9,999 shuffles can give, and Holm-corrected p = 0.0004. Half A: 71 stones, mean cos 0.45, p = 0.0001. Half B: 52 stones, mean cos 0.26, p = 0.019. H2 *holds* by the plan's rule. In plain words: of the stones where we know where the road ran, half turn their text towards the road, within 45 degrees either way; if the direction were random, a quarter would.

:::chart Inscription turned within 45 degrees of the road, percent
+All stones with a road | 49.6 | 123 stones
Road from the register text | 62.3 | 69 stones
Registered route within 500 m | 27.5 | 80 stones
Expected if the direction were random | 25.0 |
Source: the Swedish register of ancient monuments and Rundata; the locked analysis. Chart: Vitki.
:::

![Figure 1](/figurer/679795656bfb2a96.webp)
Figure 1. Left, the measure: the angle v between the direction the inscription faces and the direction to the road. Right, the 123 stones: 31 face the same compass point as the road (within 11.25 degrees), against about 8 if the direction were random. Illustration and chart: Vitki, from the Swedish register of ancient monuments and Rundata.

**5.2 The compass, the farm and the bridges (H1, H3, H4).** The directions do not differ detectably from an even spread over the compass: Rayleigh's test p = 0.49 (in half A p = 0.79, in half B p = 0.039: half B on its own leans towards the south-west, but neither half A nor the whole material does, so by the plan's rule it does not count). West is the most common (37 stones), then north (26), east (25) and south (25); 32 percent face somewhere between south-east and south-west, about what an even spread gives (31 percent, five of the sixteen points). Towards the farm: mean cos 0.01 against −0.02, p = 0.30; so we found no sign that the inscription was turned towards the farm, but the farm sites are known only from the maps of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The bridge and road stones (9 with a road) do not differ detectably from other stones, p = 0.86, but with nine stones the test says little. None of the three hypotheses holds.

**The plan's robustness tests.** With the farm within 500 metres instead of one kilometre (52 stones): mean cos 0.01 against −0.06, p = 0.20. With only Uppland and Södermanland (92 stones with a road): mean cos 0.35 against −0.02, p = 0.0001, 52 percent within 45 degrees. The plan's two other tests, only roads from the register text and only registered routes and road markers, are among the sensitivity analyses in 5.3.

**5.3 The sensitivity analyses.** All hold:

- Half A (71 stones): mean cos 0.45 against 0.04, p = 0.0001.
- Half B (52 stones): mean cos 0.26 against 0.05, p = 0.016.
- Without one province at a time: without Uppland (62 stones left, half, so only the direction is required) mean cos 0.50, p = 0.0001; without Södermanland (92) 0.29, p = 0.0001; without Östergötland (113) 0.36, p = 0.0001.
- The parish as the unit, 76 parishes (123 stones): mean cos 0.36 against 0.02, p = 0.0001.
- One stone per secure carver, 20 carvers (93 stones): mean cos 0.38 against 0.03, p = 0.0001.
- Without re-erected stones, 14 removed (109 stones): mean cos 0.43 against 0.02, p = 0.0001.
- Without stones Runor gives as moved, 10 removed (113 stones): mean cos 0.35 against 0.01, p = 0.0001.
- With the rule for moved stones after the correction of 27 October 2026 none of the 123 counts as moved, since the main analysis is already built on that rule; the result is the same as the main test.
- Only roads from the register text, 62 percent within 45 degrees (69 stones): mean cos 0.49 against 0.07, p = 0.0001.
- Only registered routes and road markers, 28 percent within 45 degrees (80 stones): mean cos 0.16 against 0.01, p = 0.020.

The sensitivity analyses drew new shuffles, so the p values differ slightly from those of the main test: half B has p = 0.016 here and p = 0.019 in 5.1. The addendum plan's word list for re-erected stones hits 29 of all 219 stones; the check after the main run, with a wider word list, hit 58. Both give the same result.

## 6. Discussion

**What the finding says.** Those who raised the runestones turned the text towards the road. It holds in the whole material, in each half, without Uppland, parish by parish and with one stone per carver, so it does not depend on a few places or workshops. It also holds without the stones that have been re-erected, which could otherwise have been turned towards today's road, and when the coding errors in 4.5 are corrected. We found no consistent sign that the inscription was turned towards a particular point of the compass or towards the farm. That does not mean there was no such association: the farm sites are known only from the maps of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and Rayleigh's test detects only a single preferred direction, not, for example, two opposite ones.

**Against earlier research.** The result gives a measure across the whole material to what Ekholm (1950) saw at single stones and to the idea that the stones by the roads were raised to be seen (Bollaert 2016). It does not contradict that many stones were raised at grave fields (Klos 2009): a stone can stand at a grave field and turn its text towards the road past it, as Ekholm (1950, p. 138) described the stone at Bollsta. The waterways are not measured here; McLeod (2014) shows that U 170 turns its text towards a former bay and has the road behind it.

**Weaknesses, in order of weight.**

1. **The road is often today's road.** The register text gives the road at the time of the survey. The association is strongest with roads from the register text (62 percent within 45 degrees) and weak with registered older routes and road markers (28 percent against 25 expected, p = 0.020). If roads were later laid past the stones, or stones were reset to face a newer road, the association with today's road may be stronger than with the Viking-Age one.
2. **The selection.** Only 214 stones in place have a single direction in the register, and we do not know what decided which stones received such a statement.
3. **Re-erections.** The word search does not catch every stone that has been re-erected, and a re-erection can turn a stone (Ekholm 1950, p. 140). The result is, however, stronger without the stones it finds, not weaker.
4. **The farm.** The farm sites are known only from the maps of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and the Viking-Age farms may have lain elsewhere. That we found no association with the farm therefore says less than the association with the road.
5. **The resolution.** The directions are given in sixteen compass points, that is in steps of 22.5 degrees.

**What would overturn the finding.** If the association disappeared when the roads were measured on the oldest land-survey maps, or if a new survey of more stones' directions gave an even distribution relative to the road.

## 7. Conclusion

The runestones turned their text towards the road: half of the inscriptions face within 45 degrees of the road, against a quarter if the direction were random, and the association withstands every sensitivity analysis, also when the coding errors are corrected. The carvers wrote for those who passed by. The next step is to measure the roads on the maps of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

## Data and code

The analysis was made in Vitki 3.0.0 (git tag v3.0.0, 2026-10-20), an open research tool for runestones ([vitkirunor.se](https://vitkirunor.se/en)), with the changes made after that version. Code state: the main analysis in commit 74ca1ef (2026-10-29), the sensitivity analyses in d0f5a6b (2026-10-31) and report version 2 in 4f80a63 (2026-11-01); the check in 4.5 was added with report version 3 in commit 6eae0af (2026-11-05), together with the builder of that version. All code, the analysis plans and the result files are openly available on [GitHub](https://github.com/Precatio/runes) under GPL-3.0.

- The corpus: Rundata, frozen for the analysis as corpus `3f58e9339191761e` (2026-10-28), with the rule for moved stones after the correction of 27 October 2026 (commit 07d2ec0). The step with that rule in 5.3 reads corpus `e83202e01a5e6d27`, which has the same rows.
- The analysis plans: `analysplaner/2026-10-29-ristningens-riktning.md` and `analysplaner/2026-10-31-riktning-trappan.md`, with their checksums in the `.sha256` files beside them.
- The analysis: `utdata/riktning/analys.py` (results `riktning.json`, the stones in `stenar.csv`); the sensitivity analyses `utdata/riktning/trappa.py` (`trappan.json`).
- The check in 4.5: `utdata/riktning/gon_kontroll.py` (`gon_kontroll.json`) reads the gon qualifiers, counts each stone once and reruns every sensitivity analysis; with the old directions it reproduces `trappan.json` exactly.
- The register: the Swedish National Heritage Board's register of ancient monuments via K-samsök (CC0); the roads come from there only. The files in `data/raa/` are not under version control but are fetched with `scripts/fetch_kmr_runstenar.py` (the runestone records, fetched 2026-10-29), `scripts/fetch_raa_remains.py` (routes, 2026-10-12) and `scripts/fetch_raa_extra.sh` (road markers and farm sites, 2026-10-29); Runor with `scripts/fetch_runor.py` (2026-10-16). The checksums of the fetched files are in `gon_kontroll.json`.
- The report is built by `utdata/blogg/build/build_rapport_riktning.py`, which reads every number from the result files and stops if anything disagrees.

## References

- Bollaert, J. 2016. *Runstenar längs vägen. En undersökning av samband mellan runstenarnas placering och utformning*. Master's thesis. Uppsala: Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University.
- Ekholm, G. 1950. Var restes runstenarna? *Fornvännen* 45, pp. 137–147.
- Holm, S. 1979. A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. *Scandinavian Journal of Statistics* 6 (2), pp. 65–70.
- Klos, L. 2009. *Runensteine in Schweden. Studien zu Aufstellungsort und Funktion*. Ergänzungsbände zum Reallexikon der Germanischen Altertumskunde 64. Berlin: de Gruyter.
- Larsson, M. G. 2010. Review of L. Klos, *Runensteine in Schweden. Studien zu Aufstellungsort und Funktion*. *Futhark. International Journal of Runic Studies* 1, pp. 249–253.
- Mardia, K. V. & Jupp, P. E. 2000. *Directional Statistics*. Chichester: Wiley.
- McLeod, S. 2014. The rediscovery of U 170: runestones, churchyards, and burial grounds in Sweden. *Journal of the North Atlantic* 25, pp. 1–8. doi:10.3721/037.006.2503
- Swedish National Heritage Board. The register of ancient monuments (Kulturmiljöregistret), via K-samsök. CC0. Retrieved 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-29.
- Swedish National Heritage Board. 2020. *Runor*. Runic inscriptions in Sweden, database. Retrieved 2026-10-16.
- Scandinavian Runic-text Database (Rundata). Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University. Open Database License.
- Zachrisson, T. 1998. *Gård, gräns, gravfält. Sammanhang kring ädelmetalldepåer och runstenar från vikingatid och tidig medeltid i Uppland och Gästrikland*. Stockholm Studies in Archaeology 15. Stockholm: Stockholm University.

:::box The essentials
- The runestones turned their text towards the road. We saw no consistent sign that the compass or the farm decided how they were turned.
- The carvers wrote for those who passed by: the stone was a message to travellers, not only a memorial by the home.
- It withstands every check we have, but the road in the register is often today's road, so the next test is the old maps.
:::

## Change log

- **Version 1, 2026-10-31.** First published version.
- **Version 2, 2026-11-01.** Figure 1 added: a sketch of the measure and a rose diagram of how the inscriptions face relative to the road. No numbers, interpretations or conclusions have changed.
- **Version 3, 2026-11-05.** Corrections after a review before permanent archiving in Zenodo; errors are corrected openly in a new version, not silently. (1) Two coding errors in how the register text was read are reported in 4.5 with a check made afterwards: gon qualifiers in nine road bearings and six inscription bearings were read as a single compass point, and five stones with two records in the register were counted twice. Corrected, the association is slightly stronger and every sensitivity analysis holds; the locked analysis's numbers stand unchanged, and the abstract and the material section say so. (2) The null results for the compass, the farm and the bridge and road stones are described as no difference detected, not as facts; the weaknesses have a point on the age of the farm sites, and the weakness on the age of the road now says that the association with registered older routes is weak. (3) Earlier research: Ekholm (1950) had already described stones turned towards the road and a re-erection that turned a stone; the objection to Klos is now attributed to Mats G. Larsson (2010), added to the references; the pages for Ekholm and McLeod are given; a reference not cited in the text is removed. (4) The plan's two robustness tests that were not reported (the farm within 500 metres, only Uppland and Södermanland) are in 5.2. (5) Form: the share facing south is described as what it counts (between south-east and south-west), 5.3 says that the sensitivity analyses drew new shuffles, the caption of Figure 1 says what the same compass point means, minus signs, the chart's maker, and under Data and code the corpus versions, commits, fetch scripts and fetch dates for the register.
- **Version 4, 2026-11-05.** A second review before archiving in Zenodo checked what version 3 changed; no numbers of the analysis have changed. (1) The objection to Klos is given more exactly: Larsson (2010) objects on p. 252 that the grave fields are overstated, and on p. 250 he notes that Klos's criteria for an ancient road were more restrictive than in his own earlier survey, not than in earlier research in general. (2) The null result for the compass is described as no consistent sign: 5.2 now explains that half B on its own leans towards the south-west (p = 0.039) but neither half A nor the whole material does, and the discussion names why the tests of the compass and the farm say less (the age of the farm sites, and that Rayleigh's test detects only a single preferred direction) instead of calling them weaker without a measure; the opening summary and the essentials box say the same. (3) The share facing between south-east and south-west (32 percent) is compared with the 31 percent an even spread gives. (4) 5.1 says that the 123 with a road are records for 120 stones. (5) In 4.5, half B's p value with each stone counted once is 0.0075, which was printed as 0.007 through a rounding error; it is now 0.008. (6) Data and code gives the commit of the check in 4.5 and the builder of version 3 (6eae0af). (7) Changes that version 3 made but did not log: the weakness on the age of the road no longer says that a later road can only weaken the association, since a road laid past the stones or a stone reset to face a newer road could also strengthen it; 5.2 gives Rayleigh's test in each half; the step with the corrected rule for moved stones says that the main analysis already uses that rule, and 4.4 and 5.3 name the rule by the date of its correction; the sentence under Data and code about a future release with a DOI is removed.
posts.author: Viktor Kvant

posts.title: Språk och innehåll ordnar Upplands runstenar i samma följd som stilkronologin – rangkorrelation 0,54 utan ornamentiken
posts.summary: Delvis prövat fynd. Ordnas Upplands runstenar bara efter språk, formler och innehåll hamnar de i ungefär samma följd som i Gräslunds stilkronologi, som bygger på ornamentiken. Det håller lika starkt i båda halvorna av materialet. I Södermanland finns samma samband, men svagare och delvis geografiskt. Inom en och samma ristare är det svagt.
posts.body:
*Viktor Kvant, oberoende forskare. Delvis prövat fynd. Rapportversion 4, 2026-11-05 (först publicerad 2026-10-31). Tidslinje: seriationen gjordes första gången 2026-10-05; materialet frystes 2026-10-29; planen för halvorna och Södermanland låstes och kördes 2026-10-31. Analysen är gjord i Vitki 3.0.0. Licens CC BY 4.0. Den engelska versionen är den kanoniska för citering: Kvant, V. (2026). Language and content order the runestones of Uppland in the same sequence as the stylistic chronology – rank correlation 0.54 without the ornament. Research report, report version 4; analysis in Vitki 3.0.0. https://vitkirunor.se/en/forskningsrapporter/seriationen-foljer-stilkronologin. Nyckelord: runstenar, vikingatid, seriation, korrespondensanalys, stilkronologi, datering, Uppland, Södermanland. Konkurrerande intressen: inga. Finansiering: ingen.*

## Sammanfattning

**Vad som inte är prövat.** Seriationen i Uppland var inte förregistrerad. Av den fasta serien känslighetsanalyser är bara halvorna prövade, under en plan som låstes före körningen tillsammans med en replikering i Södermanland; ristaren och socknen som slumpeffekter, läget som rumslig yta, analysen utan flyttade stenar och modellkontrollen är inte prövade.
**Bakgrund och syfte.** Upplands runstenar dateras relativt efter ornamentiken, enligt Anne-Sofie Gräslunds stilkronologi. Frågan här är om stenarna hamnar i samma följd när de ordnas efter något annat: språket, formlerna och innehållet.
**Material.** 818 runstenar i Uppland med minst fyra av 65 drag, varav 501 med stilgrupp; för replikeringen 270 stenar i Södermanland, varav 151 med stilgrupp. Ur Samnordisk runtextdatabas (Rundata). Seriationen görs på Uppland, eftersom dess första axel i hela det svenska materialet främst följer regionala skillnader.
**Metod.** Korrespondensanalys av en tabell över stenar och drag, utan stilgruppen; stenarnas läge på första axeln jämförs med stilgruppens mittår (Spearmans rangkorrelation). Halvorna och Södermanland med samma metod, Holm-korrigerat.
**Resultat.** I Uppland rho = 0,54, 0,54 med latituden konstant. Halva A 0,51, halva B 0,54, båda Holm-korrigerat p under 10⁻¹⁷. Södermanland 0,32, Holm-korrigerat p = 6,3 · 10⁻⁵, men 0,29 med latituden konstant. Inom härad 0,51, inom samma ristare bara 0,25.
**Slutsats.** Språk och innehåll bär samma tidsföljd som ornamentiken i Uppland. Det är ett stöd för stilkronologin som inte bygger på ornamentiken. Inom en och samma ristare är sambandet svagt, men varje ristares stenar spänner över kort tid, så materialet kan inte avgöra hur mycket av överensstämmelsen som går via ristarna. Det räcker inte för att datera enskilda stenar.

## 1. Inledning

Upplands vikingatida runstenar dateras relativt efter ornamentiken, i Anne-Sofie Gräslunds stilgrupper från RAK och Fp till Pr1–Pr5 (Gräslund 2006). Kronologin bygger på hur runormen och djurhuvudena är formade, inte på språket eller vad texten säger. Om språk och innehåll förändrades under samma tid borde stenarna hamna i ungefär samma följd när de ordnas efter dem. Ger två slags iakttagelser samma ordning följer båda troligen tiden – om de inte båda följer något tredje, till exempel ristaren.

Enskilda drag har tidigare ställts mot stilgrupperna, till exempel hur ʀ skrivs i Södermanland och Uppland stilgrupp för stilgrupp (Larsson 2002, tabell 6–9). Seriation med korrespondensanalys är en vanlig metod för relativ datering i arkeologin (Greenacre 2007). Vi har inte funnit någon studie som ordnar många drag på en gång, utan ornamentiken, och prövar ordningen i två halvor av materialet och i ett andra landskap, Södermanland, där kronologin inte byggdes.

## 2. Förregistrering: vad som var bestämt i förväg och vad som är explorativt

Seriationen i Uppland gjordes första gången den 5 oktober 2026 som en del av projektets genomgång, utan låst plan, och dess värde var känt när resten av studien planerades. Den är alltså inte förregistrerad. Samma genomgång hade visat att seriationens första axel i hela det svenska materialet följer regionala skillnader (3), och därför gjordes den på Uppland. Varianterna utan kors, utan utlandsfärder och utan de drag som förändras över tid, och korrelationerna inom härad och ristare (5.3), räknades samtidigt och är explorativa.

Den 31 oktober 2026 låstes en plan för två prövningar innan de kördes (kontrollsumma SHA-256 `454cacf9d8185a26…`): seriationen i var halva av Upplands stenar för sig, och samma seriation på Södermanlands stenar, som inte hade seriationsprövats för sig. Halvorna håller när Holm-p är under 0,05 och rho minst 0,3 i båda. Södermanland är *replikerat* med samma gränser; är korrelationen med latituden konstant under 0,3 sägs att sambandet kan vara geografiskt. En provkörning återgav Upplands kända värde exakt innan prövningarna kördes.

## 3. Material

- **Källa.** Samnordisk runtextdatabas, Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet: Rundata (utgåvan 2014, uppdaterad 2018), hämtad 2026-10-04; härledd korpus beräknad 2026-10-29. Bara runstenar.
- **Dragen.** Språkdrag (stavning av vissa ljud och ord), fem formler (resarformel, monument, ordföljd, ristarsignatur, bön), kors, kortkvistrunor och innehållskategorier, som närvaro eller frånvaro per sten. Drag som finns på färre än 15 stenar räknas inte, och stenar med färre än fyra drag räknas inte. Stilgruppen ingår inte.
- **Tiden** är stilgruppens mittår enligt Gräslund (2006).
- **Varför Uppland.** I hela det svenska materialet (1 629 stenar med minst fyra drag) följer seriationens första axel främst regionala skillnader och ristarna, och bara svagt tiden (rangkorrelation med stilgruppens mittår 0,17); den andra axeln följer tiden bättre (0,59), men också landskap och ristare. Därför görs seriationen på Uppland, där stilkronologin byggdes.
- **Uppland:** 818 stenar och 65 drag, 501 stenar med stilgrupp. **Södermanland:** 270 stenar och 44 drag, 151 med stilgrupp.
- **Halvorna** är projektets fasta indelning socken för socken.

## 4. Metod

**4.1 Seriationen.** Korrespondensanalys (paketet ca; Nenadić & Greenacre 2007) av tabellen med stenar och drag. Analysen placerar stenar som har samma drag nära varandra, och drag som brukar finnas på samma stenar nära varandra; den första axeln är den riktning i materialet som skiljer stenarna mest. Stenarnas läge på den första axeln jämförs med stilgruppens mittår med Spearmans rangkorrelation. Axelns tecken är godtyckligt och vänds så att korrelationen blir positiv.

**4.2 Geografin.** Eftersom språkdrag också skiljer sig mellan norr och söder redovisas den partiella korrelationen med latituden konstant.

**4.3 Halvorna och Södermanland.** Samma metod, oförändrad, på var halva och på Södermanland, Holm-korrigerat över de tre testen.

**4.4 Varianterna (explorativa).** Seriationen utan draget kors, utan draget utlandsfärd, utan de drag vars förändring över tid mäts för sig (stungna runor, monoftongen, åsrunan) och utan allt detta; varianterna tar bort dragen, inte stenarna. Därtill korrelationen inom härad och inom ristare med minst fem daterade stenar.

**4.5 Avvikelser.** Inga från planen.

## 5. Resultat

**5.1 Uppland och halvorna.** I Uppland är rho = 0,54 (okorrigerat p = 9,4 · 10⁻⁴⁰) och 0,54 med latituden konstant; latituden själv korrelerar bara 0,09 med axeln. Halva A: 264 daterade stenar, rho 0,51, med latituden konstant 0,51. Halva B: 236 daterade stenar, rho 0,54, med latituden konstant 0,53. Båda Holm-korrigerat p under 10⁻¹⁷: halvorna *håller*. Stilgrupperna i medel längs axeln: RAK -0,79, Fp -0,89, Pr1 -0,46, Pr2 -0,18, Pr3 -0,01, Pr4 0,51, Pr5 0,80: följden är stilkronologins, utom att RAK och Fp byter plats. I klartext: ordnar man stenarna bara efter vad och hur det står skrivet hamnar de i ungefär samma ordning som när man ordnar dem efter ornamentiken; sambandet är måttligt starkt och lika starkt i båda halvorna.

![Figur 1](/figurer/9834659d1c7489d9.webp)
**Figur 1.** Upplands 501 stildaterade runstenar, ordnade bara efter språk och innehåll, mot stilgruppen. Varje punkt är en sten och strecket mittvärdet i gruppen: ordningen stiger med stilgrupperna, men spridningen inom varje grupp är stor. Diagram: Vitki, efter Rundata (ODbL); stilgrupperna efter Gräslund (2006).

**5.2 Södermanland (replikering).** 151 daterade stenar: rho 0,32, Holm-korrigerat p = 6,3 · 10⁻⁵; *replikerat* enligt planens regel. Med latituden konstant 0,29, under planens gräns 0,3, så sambandet kan delvis vara geografiskt. Inom härad 0,24 (11 härader).

**5.3 Känslighetsanalyserna steg för steg.** Projektets fasta serie känslighetsanalyser är byggd för samband mellan två drag och har inte körts på seriationen. Steg för steg, med det som kommer närmast:

- Halvorna: prövat (5.1); håller.
- Justerat för landskapet: inte prövat; seriationen görs inom ett landskap, och Södermanland prövas för sig (5.2).
- Ristaren som slumpeffekt: inte prövat. Närmast kommer korrelationen inom ristare: bara 0,25 (13 ristare med minst fem daterade stenar, 251 stenar; explorativ). Av spridningen i datering mellan dessa stenar ligger bara 18 procent inom ristarna (räknat på stenarnas rangordning i tid); resten skiljer ristarna åt, så inom en ristare finns lite tid att mäta.
- Socknen som slumpeffekt: inte prövat. Närmast kommer korrelationen inom härad: 0,51 (23 härader; explorativ).
- Läget som rumslig yta: inte prövat. Närmast kommer den partiella korrelationen med latituden konstant: 0,54.
- Utan ett landskap i taget: inte tillämpligt, eftersom seriationen gäller ett landskap; i stället replikeringen i Södermanland.
- Utan flyttade stenar: inte prövat.
- Modellkontroll: inte prövat; korrespondensanalysen har ingen motsvarande kontroll av residualerna.
- Justering tillsammans med alla 48 samband som projektet redovisar: gjord, med seriationens eget p eftersom den saknar känslighetsanalyser av det slaget; q < 0,001. Holm-korrigeringen gäller planens tre test.
- Varianterna av dragen (explorativa): utan kors 0,55, utan utlandsfärd 0,54, utan de drag som förändras över tid 0,54, utan allt detta 0,53.

**5.4 Dateringen av enskilda stenar.** Används axeln för att skatta årtal blir medelfelet 21 år när varje sten skattas utan sig själv, mot 25 år för att gissa medelåret: seriationen ordnar stenarna, men den daterar inte en enskild sten mycket bättre än en gissning.

## 6. Diskussion

**Vad fyndet säger.** Språket, formlerna och innehållet förändrades i samma följd som ornamentiken i Uppland, och det håller lika starkt i två halvor av materialet. Eftersom ornamentiken inte ingår är det ett stöd för Gräslunds relativa kronologi som inte bygger på ornamentiken; hur mycket av det som går via ristarna kan materialet inte avgöra (5.3). Det står sig också utan korsen, som är en del av bilden, utan draget utlandsfärd (som Ingvars- och Englandsstenarna bär och som annars kunde förankra tiden) och utan de stavningsdrag vars förändring mäts för sig.

**Mot tidigare forskning.** Stilkronologin är den grund de flesta dateringar av svenska runstenar vilar på (Gräslund 2006). Resultatet säger att den inte bara är en ordning av ornament: språk och innehåll följer samma tid. I Södermanland, där kronologin tillämpas men inte byggdes, finns samma följd men drygt hälften så stark.

**Svagheter, i ordning efter vikt.**

1. **Följden är svag inom ristare.** Inom en och samma ristare är korrelationen bara 0,25. Ornament och språk följer båda ristaren, och ristarna verkade vid olika tider; en del av överensstämmelsen kan därför vara att seriationen ordnar ristare. Men varje ristares stenar spänner över kort tid (18 procent av spridningen i datering ligger inom ristarna, och 2 av de 13 ristarna har stenar i en enda stilgrupp), så en svag korrelation inom ristare väntas också om språket följer tiden. Inom härad står den sig (0,51), så det är inte en ordning av bygder.
2. **Inte förregistrerad.** Seriationen i Uppland var känd när planen för halvorna och Södermanland låstes, och valet av Uppland gjordes efter att hela materialet visat en regional första axel. Halvorna och Södermanland är därför det egentliga provet.
3. **Södermanland kan vara geografi.** Med latituden konstant är korrelationen 0,29, under planens gräns.
4. **Inte en datering.** Medelfelet för årtal är bara något bättre än att gissa medelåret.

**Vad som skulle fälla fyndet.** Att korrelationen försvann inom ristare också i ett större material med fler ristare som verkade länge, eller att en datering oberoende av både ornament och språk gav en annan följd.

## 7. Slutsats

Ordnade efter språk, formler och innehåll hamnar Upplands runstenar i samma följd som i stilkronologin, rho 0,54, och det håller i båda halvorna. Det är ett stöd för den relativa kronologin som inte bygger på ornamentiken; hur mycket av det som går via ristarna kan materialet inte avgöra, och i Södermanland är sambandet svagare och delvis geografiskt. Nästa steg är att pröva seriationen inom ristare som verkade under lång tid, och i Östergötland och Västergötland när dateringen där blir säkrare.

## Data och kod

Analysen är gjord i Vitki 3.0.0, ett öppet forskningsverktyg för runstenar ([vitkirunor.se](https://vitkirunor.se)). Kodläge: commit 4f80a63 i https://github.com/Precatio/runes (Vitki 3.0.0 med senare ändringar); rapportens byggare för versionerna 2026-11-05 från commit 6eae0af. Koden, analysplanen och resultatfilerna finns där under GPL-3.0.

- Seriationen: `r/chronology.R` (resultat `chronology.json` under materialets version `e83202e01a5e6d27`).
- Planen för halvorna och Södermanland: `analysplaner/2026-10-31-seriation-halvor-sodermanland.md`; koden `utdata/seriation/replikering.R`, resultaten `replikering.json` och `replikering_resultat.md`.
- Rapporten byggs av `utdata/blogg/build/build_rapport_seriation.py`, som läser alla tal ur resultatfilerna och stannar om något inte stämmer.
- I Vitki visas seriationen under Statistik, Datering. Ordlista över de statistiska begreppen: https://vitkirunor.se/forskningsrapporter/begrepp.

## Referenser

- Greenacre, M. 2007. *Correspondence Analysis in Practice*. 2 uppl. Boca Raton: Chapman & Hall/CRC.
- Gräslund, A.-S. 2006. Dating the Swedish Viking-Age rune stones on stylistic grounds. I: M. Stoklund m.fl. (red.), *Runes and their Secrets: Studies in Runology*. Köpenhamn: Museum Tusculanum Press, s. 117–139.
- Holm, S. 1979. A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. *Scandinavian Journal of Statistics* 6 (2), s. 65–70.
- Kvant, V. 2026. *Vitki 3.0.0: metodbeskrivning* (METHODS.md). https://github.com/Precatio/runes
- Larsson, P. 2002. *Yrrunan. Användning och ljudvärde i nordiska runinskrifter*. Runrön 17. Uppsala: Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet.
- Nenadić, O. & Greenacre, M. 2007. Correspondence analysis in R, with two- and three-dimensional graphics: the ca package. *Journal of Statistical Software* 20 (3).
- Samnordisk runtextdatabas (Rundata), utgåvan 2014, uppdaterad 2018. Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet. https://www.nordiska.uu.se/forskn/samnord.htm, hämtad 2026-10-04. Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0 / Database Contents License (DbCL) 1.0.

:::box Det viktigaste i korthet
- Det som står på stenarna förändrades i samma ordning som ornamentiken.
- Det ger stilkronologin ett stöd som inte bygger på ornamenten själva.
- Inom en och samma ristare är ordningen svag, men en ristares stenar spänner över kort tid, så det säger lite. Ordningen räcker inte för att datera en enskild sten.
:::

## Ändringslogg

- **Version 2, 2026-11-01.** Figur 1 tillagd: varje stildaterad sten i Uppland, ordnad efter språk och innehåll, mot stilgruppen. Inga siffror, tolkningar eller slutsatser är ändrade.
- **Version 3, 2026-11-05.** Rättelser efter granskningen före arkiveringen i Zenodo. Varianten utan utlandsfärder tar bort draget utlandsfärd, inte Ingvars- och Englandsstenarna, som texten sa. Att seriationens första axel i hela det svenska materialet följer regionala skillnader och bara svagt tiden, skälet till att den görs på Uppland, var utelämnat. ”Oberoende stöd” och ”två oberoende klockor” sa mer än materialet bär, eftersom korrelationen inom ristare bara är 0,25. Södermanlands samband är drygt, inte ungefär, hälften så starkt. De känslighetsanalyser som inte är prövade räknas nu upp steg för steg (5.3, som har bytt plats med Södermanland enligt mallen), och tidigare forskning om enskilda drag mot stilgrupperna nämns. Diagrammet med rangkorrelationerna visade dem som procent och är struket; talen står i texten. Kodläge, dataversioner, absoluta länkar och källa i bildtexten är tillagda. Inga analyser är omgjorda och inga tidigare siffror ändrade.
- **Version 4, 2026-11-05.** Rättelser efter en andra granskning före arkiveringen i Zenodo. Justeringen för alla 48 samband som projektet redovisar sades vara inte prövad; den är gjord, med seriationens eget p, och ger q < 0,001 (sammanfattningen och 5.3). ”Till stor del via ristarna” sa mer än materialet bär: varje ristares stenar spänner över kort tid (bara 18 procent av spridningen i datering ligger inom ristarna, och 2 av 13 ristare har stenar i en enda stilgrupp), så en svag korrelation inom ristare väntas också om språket följer tiden; det står nu i sammanfattningen, diskussionen, svaghet 1, slutsatsen och korthetsrutan. Version 3 lade utan att säga det till att det är nytt att ordna många drag på en gång; det står nu som att vi inte har funnit någon sådan studie. Den engelska meningen om varför seriationen görs på Uppland var tvetydig om ristarna. Kodläget anger nu också den commit där rapportens byggare finns. Inga analyser är omgjorda; andelen 18 procent är räknad ur seriationens egna resultat, och inga tidigare siffror är ändrade.
posts.title_en: Language and content order the runestones of Uppland in the same sequence as the stylistic chronology – rank correlation 0.54 without the ornament
posts.summary_en: Partially tested finding. If the runestones of Uppland are ordered only by language, formulas and content, they fall in roughly the same sequence as in Gräslund's stylistic chronology, which rests on the ornament. It holds equally strongly in both halves of the material. In Södermanland the same association is found, but weaker and partly geographical. Within one and the same carver it is weak.
posts.body_en:
*Viktor Kvant, independent researcher. Partially tested finding. Report version 4, 2026-11-05 (first published 2026-10-31). Timeline: the seriation was first made 2026-10-05; the material was frozen 2026-10-29; the plan for the halves and Södermanland was locked and run 2026-10-31. The analysis was made in Vitki 3.0.0. Licence CC BY 4.0. This English version is the canonical one for citation: Kvant, V. (2026). Language and content order the runestones of Uppland in the same sequence as the stylistic chronology – rank correlation 0.54 without the ornament. Research report, report version 4; analysis in Vitki 3.0.0. https://vitkirunor.se/en/forskningsrapporter/seriationen-foljer-stilkronologin. Keywords: runestones, Viking Age, seriation, correspondence analysis, stylistic chronology, dating, Uppland, Södermanland. Competing interests: none. Funding: none.*

## Abstract

**What has not been tested.** The seriation in Uppland was not pre-registered. Of the fixed series of sensitivity analyses only the halves are tested, under a plan locked before the run together with a replication in Södermanland; the carver and the parish as random effects, location as a spatial surface, the analysis without moved stones and the model check are not tested.
**Background and aim.** The runestones of Uppland are dated relatively by their ornament, following Anne-Sofie Gräslund's stylistic chronology. The question here is whether the stones fall in the same sequence when ordered by something else: the language, the formulas and the content.
**Material.** 818 runestones in Uppland with at least four of 65 traits, 501 of them with a style group; for the replication 270 stones in Södermanland, 151 with a style group. From the Scandinavian Runic-text Database (Rundata). The seriation is made on Uppland, since in the whole Swedish material its first axis mainly follows regional differences.
**Method.** Correspondence analysis of a table of stones and traits, without the style group; the stones' position on the first axis is compared with the style group's midpoint (Spearman's rank correlation). The halves and Södermanland with the same method, Holm-corrected.
**Results.** In Uppland rho = 0.54, 0.54 with latitude held constant. Half A 0.51, half B 0.54, both Holm-corrected p below 10⁻¹⁷. Södermanland 0.32, Holm-corrected p = 6.3 · 10⁻⁵, but 0.29 with latitude held constant. Within hundreds 0.51, within one and the same carver only 0.25.
**Conclusion.** Language and content carry the same temporal sequence as the ornament in Uppland. That is support for the stylistic chronology that does not rest on the ornament. Within one and the same carver the association is weak, but each carver's stones span a short time, so the material cannot tell how much of the agreement runs through the carvers. It is not enough to date individual stones.

## 1. Introduction

The Viking-Age runestones of Uppland are dated relatively by their ornament, in Anne-Sofie Gräslund's style groups from RAK and Fp to Pr1–Pr5 (Gräslund 2006). The chronology rests on how the rune animal and the animal heads are shaped, not on the language or on what the text says. If language and content changed over the same time, the stones should fall in roughly the same sequence when ordered by them. If two kinds of observation give the same order, both probably follow time – unless both follow something third, such as the carver.

Single traits have earlier been set against the style groups, for instance how ʀ is written in Södermanland and Uppland style group by style group (Larsson 2002, tables 6–9). Seriation by correspondence analysis is a common method of relative dating in archaeology (Greenacre 2007). We have found no study that orders many traits at once, without the ornament, and tests the order in two halves of the material and in a second province, Södermanland, where the chronology was not built.

## 2. Pre-registration: what was fixed in advance and what is exploratory

The seriation in Uppland was first made on 5 October 2026 as part of the project's survey, without a locked plan, and its value was known when the rest of the study was planned. It is therefore not pre-registered. The same survey had shown that the seriation's first axis in the whole Swedish material follows regional differences (3), and it was therefore made on Uppland. The variants without crosses, without journeys abroad and without the traits that change over time, and the correlations within hundreds and carvers (5.3), were computed at the same time and are exploratory.

On 31 October 2026 a plan for two tests was locked before they were run (SHA-256 checksum `454cacf9d8185a26…`): the seriation in each half of the stones of Uppland on its own, and the same seriation on the stones of Södermanland, which had not been seriated on their own. The halves hold when Holm p is below 0.05 and rho at least 0.3 in both. Södermanland is *replicated* by the same limits; if the correlation with latitude held constant is below 0.3, the association is said to be possibly geographical. A trial run reproduced Uppland's known value exactly before the tests were run.

## 3. Material

- **Source.** The Scandinavian Runic-text Database, Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University: Rundata (2014 edition, updated 2018), retrieved 2026-10-04; derived corpus computed 2026-10-29. Runestones only.
- **The traits.** Language traits (the spelling of certain sounds and words), five formulas (sponsor formula, monument, word order, carver's signature, prayer), cross, short-twig runes and content categories, as presence or absence per stone. Traits found on fewer than 15 stones are not counted, nor stones with fewer than four traits. The style group is not included.
- **Time** is the style group's midpoint after Gräslund (2006).
- **Why Uppland.** In the whole Swedish material (1,629 stones with at least four traits) the seriation's first axis follows mainly regional differences and the carvers, and time only weakly (rank correlation with the style-group midpoint 0.17); the second axis follows time better (0.59), but also province and carver. The seriation is therefore made on Uppland, where the stylistic chronology was built.
- **Uppland:** 818 stones and 65 traits, 501 stones with a style group. **Södermanland:** 270 stones and 44 traits, 151 with a style group.
- **The halves** are the project's fixed division parish by parish.

## 4. Method

**4.1 The seriation.** Correspondence analysis (the package ca; Nenadić & Greenacre 2007) of the table of stones and traits. The analysis places stones that have the same traits close together, and traits that tend to occur on the same stones close together; the first axis is the direction in the material that separates the stones most. The stones' position on the first axis is compared with the style group's midpoint by Spearman's rank correlation. The sign of the axis is arbitrary and is turned so that the correlation is positive.

**4.2 The geography.** Since language traits also differ between north and south, the partial correlation with latitude held constant is reported.

**4.3 The halves and Södermanland.** The same method, unchanged, on each half and on Södermanland, Holm-corrected over the three tests.

**4.4 The variants (exploratory).** The seriation without the trait cross, without the trait journey abroad, without the traits whose change over time is measured separately (dotted runes, the monophthong, the ós-rune) and without all of these; the variants drop the traits, not the stones. In addition, the correlation within hundreds and within carvers with at least five dated stones.

**4.5 Deviations.** None from the plan.

## 5. Results

**5.1 Uppland and the halves.** In Uppland rho = 0.54 (uncorrected p = 9.4 · 10⁻⁴⁰) and 0.54 with latitude held constant; latitude itself correlates only 0.09 with the axis. Half A: 264 dated stones, rho 0.51, with latitude held constant 0.51. Half B: 236 dated stones, rho 0.54, with latitude held constant 0.53. Both Holm-corrected p below 10⁻¹⁷: the halves *hold*. The style groups on average along the axis: RAK -0.79, Fp -0.89, Pr1 -0.46, Pr2 -0.18, Pr3 -0.01, Pr4 0.51, Pr5 0.80: the sequence is that of the stylistic chronology, except that RAK and Fp change places. In plain words: if one orders the stones only by what is written and how, they fall in roughly the same order as when one orders them by the ornament; the association is moderately strong and equally strong in both halves.

![Figure 1](/figurer/1bc45732263442b3.webp)
**Figure 1.** Uppland's 501 style-dated runestones, ordered by language and content alone, against the style group. Each dot is a stone and the bar the middle value of the group: the order rises with the style groups, but the spread within each group is large. Chart: Vitki, after Rundata (ODbL); the style groups after Gräslund (2006).

**5.2 Södermanland (replication).** 151 dated stones: rho 0.32, Holm-corrected p = 6.3 · 10⁻⁵; *replicated* by the plan's rule. With latitude held constant 0.29, below the plan's limit of 0.3, so the association may be partly geographical. Within hundreds 0.24 (11 hundreds).

**5.3 The sensitivity analyses step by step.** The project's fixed series of sensitivity analyses is built for associations between two traits and has not been run on the seriation. Step by step, with what comes closest:

- The halves: tested (5.1); they hold.
- Adjusted for province: not tested; the seriation is made within one province, and Södermanland is tested on its own (5.2).
- The carver as a random effect: not tested. Closest is the correlation within carvers: only 0.25 (13 carvers with at least five dated stones, 251 stones; exploratory). Of the spread in dating among these stones only 18 percent lies within the carvers (computed on the stones' rank order in time); the rest separates the carvers, so within one carver there is little time to measure.
- The parish as a random effect: not tested. Closest is the correlation within hundreds: 0.51 (23 hundreds; exploratory).
- Location as a spatial surface: not tested. Closest is the partial correlation with latitude held constant: 0.54.
- Without one province at a time: not applicable, since the seriation concerns one province; instead the replication in Södermanland.
- Without moved stones: not tested.
- Model check: not tested; the correspondence analysis has no corresponding check of residuals.
- Adjustment together with all 48 associations the project reports: done, with the seriation's own p since it has no sensitivity analyses of that kind; q < 0.001. The Holm correction covers the plan's three tests.
- The variants of the traits (exploratory): without cross 0.55, without journey abroad 0.54, without the traits that change over time 0.54, without all of these 0.53.

**5.4 Dating individual stones.** If the axis is used to estimate years, the mean error is 21 years when each stone is estimated without itself, against 25 years for guessing the mean year: the seriation orders the stones, but it does not date a single stone much better than a guess.

## 6. Discussion

**What the finding says.** Language, formulas and content changed in the same sequence as the ornament in Uppland, and it holds equally strongly in two halves of the material. Since the ornament is not included, it is support for Gräslund's relative chronology that does not rest on the ornament; how much of it runs through the carvers the material cannot tell (5.3). It also holds without the crosses, which are part of the picture, without the trait journey abroad (which the Ingvar and England stones carry and which could otherwise anchor the time) and without the spelling traits whose change is measured separately.

**Against earlier research.** The stylistic chronology is the basis on which most datings of Swedish runestones rest (Gräslund 2006). The result says that it is not only an ordering of ornament: language and content follow the same time. In Södermanland, where the chronology is applied but was not built, the same sequence is found but a little over half as strong.

**Weaknesses, in order of weight.**

1. **The sequence is weak within carvers.** Within one and the same carver the correlation is only 0.25. Ornament and language both follow the carver, and the carvers worked at different times; part of the agreement may therefore be that the seriation orders carvers. But each carver's stones span a short time (18 percent of the spread in dating lies within the carvers, and 2 of the 13 carvers have stones in a single style group), so a weak correlation within carvers is expected even if language follows time. Within hundreds it holds (0.51), so it is not an ordering of districts.
2. **Not pre-registered.** The seriation in Uppland was known when the plan for the halves and Södermanland was locked, and Uppland was chosen after the whole material had shown a regional first axis. The halves and Södermanland are therefore the actual test.
3. **Södermanland may be geography.** With latitude held constant the correlation is 0.29, below the plan's limit.
4. **Not a dating.** The mean error for years is only somewhat better than guessing the mean year.

**What would overturn the finding.** If the correlation disappeared within carvers also in a larger material with more carvers who worked long, or if a dating independent of both ornament and language gave another sequence.

## 7. Conclusion

Ordered by language, formulas and content, the runestones of Uppland fall in the same sequence as in the stylistic chronology, rho 0.54, and it holds in both halves. That is support for the relative chronology that does not rest on the ornament; how much of it runs through the carvers the material cannot tell, and in Södermanland the association is weaker and partly geographical. The next step is to test the seriation within carvers who worked over a long time, and in Östergötland and Västergötland when the dating there becomes more secure.

## Data and code

The analysis was made in Vitki 3.0.0, an open research tool for runestones ([vitkirunor.se](https://vitkirunor.se/en)). Code state: commit 4f80a63 in https://github.com/Precatio/runes (Vitki 3.0.0 plus later changes); the report's builder for the versions of 2026-11-05 from commit 6eae0af. The code, the analysis plan and the result files are there under GPL-3.0.

- The seriation: `r/chronology.R` (results `chronology.json` under the material's version `e83202e01a5e6d27`).
- The plan for the halves and Södermanland: `analysplaner/2026-10-31-seriation-halvor-sodermanland.md`; the code `utdata/seriation/replikering.R`, the results `replikering.json` and `replikering_resultat.md`.
- The report is built by `utdata/blogg/build/build_rapport_seriation.py`, which reads every number from the result files and stops if anything disagrees.
- In Vitki the seriation is shown under Statistics, Dating. Glossary of the statistical terms: https://vitkirunor.se/en/forskningsrapporter/begrepp.

## References

- Greenacre, M. 2007. *Correspondence Analysis in Practice*. 2nd ed. Boca Raton: Chapman & Hall/CRC.
- Gräslund, A.-S. 2006. Dating the Swedish Viking-Age rune stones on stylistic grounds. In: M. Stoklund et al. (eds), *Runes and their Secrets: Studies in Runology*. Copenhagen: Museum Tusculanum Press, pp. 117–139.
- Holm, S. 1979. A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. *Scandinavian Journal of Statistics* 6 (2), pp. 65–70.
- Kvant, V. 2026. *Vitki 3.0.0: method description* (METHODS.md). https://github.com/Precatio/runes
- Larsson, P. 2002. *Yrrunan. Användning och ljudvärde i nordiska runinskrifter*. Runrön 17. Uppsala: Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University.
- Nenadić, O. & Greenacre, M. 2007. Correspondence analysis in R, with two- and three-dimensional graphics: the ca package. *Journal of Statistical Software* 20 (3).
- Scandinavian Runic-text Database (Rundata), 2014 edition, updated 2018. Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University. https://www.nordiska.uu.se/forskn/samnord.htm, retrieved 2026-10-04. Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0 / Database Contents License (DbCL) 1.0.

:::box The essentials
- What is written on the stones changed in the same order as the ornament.
- That gives the stylistic chronology support that does not rest on the ornaments themselves.
- Within one and the same carver the order is weak, but a carver's stones span a short time, so that says little. The order is not enough to date a single stone.
:::

## Change log

- **Version 2, 2026-11-01.** Figure 1 added: every style-dated stone in Uppland, ordered by language and content, against the style group. No numbers, interpretations or conclusions have changed.
- **Version 3, 2026-11-05.** Corrections after the review before archiving in Zenodo. The variant without journeys abroad drops the trait journey abroad, not the Ingvar and England stones, as the text said. That the seriation's first axis in the whole Swedish material follows regional differences and time only weakly, the reason why it is made on Uppland, was left out. ”Independent support” and ”two independent clocks” said more than the material bears, since the correlation within carvers is only 0.25. Södermanland's association is a little over, not about, half as strong. The sensitivity analyses not tested are now listed step by step (5.3, which has changed places with Södermanland as the template prescribes), and earlier research on single traits against the style groups is mentioned. The chart of the rank correlations showed them as percentages and is removed; the numbers are in the text. Code state, data versions, absolute links and a source in the caption were added. No analysis was redone and no earlier figure changed.
- **Version 4, 2026-11-05.** Corrections after a second review before archiving in Zenodo. The adjustment for all 48 associations the project reports was said not to be tested; it is done, with the seriation's own p, and gives q < 0.001 (abstract and 5.3). ”Largely through the carvers” said more than the material bears: each carver's stones span a short time (only 18 percent of the spread in dating lies within the carvers, and 2 of 13 carvers have stones in a single style group), so a weak correlation within carvers is expected even if language follows time; this now stands in the abstract, the discussion, weakness 1, the conclusion and the essentials box. Version 3 added, without saying so, that ordering many traits at once is new; it now says that we have found no such study. The English sentence on why the seriation is made on Uppland was ambiguous about the carvers. The code state now also names the commit holding the report's builder. No analysis was redone; the share of 18 percent is computed from the seriation's own results, and no earlier figure changed.
